newsitem.title: USA: Axent sees Street's 1997 estimate a bit low.
newsitem.headline: Axent sees Street's 1997 estimate a bit low.

text.p: Axent Technologies Inc management is comfortable with Wall Street's consensus estimate of $0.30 a share for 1996 earnings but believes the Street consensus for 1997 of $0.36 a share is a bit low, its president said.
John Becker, president and chief operating officer, told Reuters that management lately has begun working with analysts to guide them to be more optimistic about its 1997 earnings growth.
Axent, a maker of security software for large corporate client/server computing systems, earned $0.26 a share in 1995.
Axent executives speaking at a Montgomery Securities technology conference said sales and earnings have grown with the growth of distributed computing systems.

Especially as more companies have employees working off site and dialing in to central data systems from laptop computers and via the Internet, customers are finding security software more important, said Richard Lefebvre, chief executive officer. Axent products are the OmniGuard line of security software, the largest of which is its Enterprise Security Management. Lefebvre said most of its customers are large, multi-national and Fortune 100 companies.
